text:
incident-bot: PAGING: High token-latency & request queue growth for model redwood-xlarge in us-west-2. Trigger: queue_depth=1287 (>1200), hpa_desired=2 -> 0 (scale failure), pool_free_gpus=0. Pager: alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): I'm on the page. Affects hosted inference; some clients seeing 504s and long tails. Noted support ticket #2456 complaining about timeouts.

ben (infra): confirming: all gpu-pool nodes show allocated=100%. Autoscaler logs show quota_denied error when creating new GPU nodes. kubernetes quota may have been hit during the spike.

carla (runtime): KV cache miss rate jumped from ~5% to ~80% in the last 8m. Cold-starts for long-context requests are spiking token compute time. Warmup completion latency increased from 12s -> 48s.

alice (oncall): timeline so far: 03:12 alarm -> 03:14 autoscaler attempted scale -> 03:15 API returned quota error -> queue climbed 03:16-03:22. Customers start to surface errors 03:18.

dave (sre): pasting relevant snippets:
```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-17T03:14:12Z Attempting scale to 4 -> quota request submitted
[autoscaler] 2026-03-17T03:15:03Z ERROR: quota_denied: insufficient-project-gpus
[router] 2026-03-17T03:16:21Z queue_depth=980 -> 1287 in 6m
[runtime] 2026-03-17T03:17:00Z warmup_start id=abc123
[runtime] 2026-03-17T03:17:50Z warmup_complete id=abc123 duration=50s
```

frank (eng): here's the hpa describe and a quick grep of the scaler logs:
```
$ kubectl describe hpa inference-redwood-xlarge
Metrics: queue_depth (custom) target 200 current 1287
Events: 3m ago ScalingDisabled: quota_denied

$ tail -n 40 /var/log/autoscaler.log | grep quota
2026-03-17T03:15:03 quota check failed: limit exceeded for GPUs in us-west-2
```

carla (runtime): runtime notes: when the pool is saturated we fall back to slower CPU-pool routing for fallthrough requests, but the routing policy isn't applied to some enterprise routes. That caused disproportionate errors for those customers. Also observed per-model queue backpressure: some routes accumulate large prefix KV loads which increases warmup time.

alice (oncall): mitigation plan (live):
- short-term: enable policy fallback for enterprise routes -> allow CPU fallback for non-latency-critical endpoints (carla to flip).
- short-term: manually pre-warm 4 smaller GPU instances from spare capacity (ben to request with infra admin); start priority warmups for customers reporting errors.
- medium: request temporary quota bump with cloud infra (ben).
- notify: publish status update and call out affected customers (eve).

ben (infra): started manual spin-up request to cloud console (req-9876). If quota bump is denied we'll still be able to reclaim some capacity by evicting low-priority dedicated pools. Doing that now: evicting demo-pool-2 and reducing reserved capacity for staging.

carla (runtime): I flipped the CPU-fallback gate for enterprise routes (applied). Also started pre-warm sequence:
```
/runtimectl prewarm --model redwood-xlarge --instances 4 --priority high
```
Prewarm results: 2/4 completed in ~22s, remaining are queued behind image-pull step.

eve (support): status page draft: "We are investigating increased latencies and errors for hosted inference in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating. Some customers may experience transient 504s." Posting in 5m unless updates. Notifying top customers now.

frank (eng): hypothesis tracker:
- H1: sudden traffic spike + cache coldness -> warmup overwhelmed -> queue growth.
- H2: autoscaler quota denial prevented capacity growth -> sustained saturation.
- H3: routing policy prevented CPU fallback for some enterprise routes -> customer-visible errors.
We should validate with request rate graphs, KV cache miss rate, and autoscaler error events.

alice (oncall): validating metrics: request rate rose ~1.8x at 03:11, KV miss rate aligns with spike, autoscaler quota errors present. H1+H2+H3 all contributing.

ben (infra): quota bump requested via support ticket cloud-12345, ETA 30-45m. Meanwhile evictions freed 2 GPUs, manual pre-warm got one extra instance online. Queue depth dropping from 1287 -> 660 after fallbacks and pre-warm.

carla (runtime): warmup latency for requests that hit pre-warmed instances back to ~14s. Routes with CPU fallback showing reduced 5xx. KV cache priming task queued to pre-populate top prefixes for affected tenants.

alice (oncall): customer impact update: partial recovery: critical customers A,B still seeing occasional 504s but overall success rate improved from 72% -> 92% in last 10m. Continuing to monitor until quota bump or autoscaler recovery.

dave (sre): handoff plan: I'm taking the bridge for the next 30m to watch autoscaler and queue metrics. alice handing off at 03:35 -> dave (sre). Notes: follow up on quota ticket, confirm eviction didn't violate SLA, track KV priming progress.

alice (oncall): handing off to dave for ongoing mitigation. Leaving these notes in incident doc: timeline, logs, hypothesis list, mitigation steps taken. If anything new surfaces ping me.

eve (support): sent update to affected customers and opened follow-up tickets to verify no data loss.

incident-bot: INCIDENCE UPDATE: Post-mitigation monitoring in progress. Current queue_depth=312, pool_free_gpus=1, warmup_median=18s. Continue bridge until stable.

frank (eng): suggestion for long-term: add a pre-emptive warmup policy when queue_depth > 150 for 2m, and have autoscaler escalate quota requests automatically. Also mark critical enterprise routes to allow CPU fallback by default during scale events.

dave (sre): ack. Will file follow-ups and include recommended runbook updates. Closing bridge when queue_depth <200 for 15m and no autoscaler errors in logs.

alice (oncall): thanks all. Good incident coordination.
